title: How do you let AI characters improvise without rewriting a mystery?
author: Maniaclord
selftext:
I'm making EKO, a browser mystery inside a missing woman's phone. Players can type their own questions to her contacts and to the assistant still answering on it.



My design problem is separating conversational freedom from story authority. The model may vary wording, emotion and evasiveness, but it cannot invent a clue, relationship or solution. A request includes the character's knowledge and only the evidence unlocked so far. Replies are checked for spoilers, identity mistakes and contradictions. Progression uses fixed events rather than whatever the model happens to say.



The tradeoff is that rejecting a more expressive reply can sometimes make the replacement feel restrained. How do others balance an AI character's freedom with fixed canon in a mystery?



The free first chapter is playable if you want to see this in context: [https://eko-kapitel-1.emmyw.chatgpt.site/?source=reddit\_aigamedev](https://eko-kapitel-1.emmyw.chatgpt.site/?source=reddit_aigamedev)



Character replies, images and voices use generative AI. The game has psychological horror and brief unsettling effects, but no graphic content in this post.
